learning_outcomes.text: Students who have successfully completed this module know various methods and software tools for analytical and constructive quality assurance.

Students who have successfully studied this module can apply various methods and software tools for analytical and constructive quality assurance; they can evaluate which methods can be efficiently used for specific types of software, taking into account other boundary conditions.

Students who have successfully studied this module have detailed knowledge and understanding of different analytical and constructive quality assurance methods, can compare their benefits, and can use them with software tools.

Students who have successfully studied this module can argue what needs to be considered from a quality assurance perspective to carry out successful software development projects. They can argue under which conditions which test approach is most promising for a project.
Students can help shape the quality assurance process depending on individual project requirements and later evaluate the results.
Students learn how customer requirements can be systematically checked with quality assurance approaches.

Students who have successfully completed this module know different techniques, algorithmic ideas for planning quality assurance measures, as well as the design, execution, and evaluation of tests. They are able to choose a suitable type of quality assurance for various types of software, and to determine and use the tools to be deployed. The procedures are practiced with examples from different application areas.

syllabus_topics: Testing of user interfaces and web applications

assessment_methods.method: experimental work (weekly assignments with practice tasks)

assessment_rules: The form of examination (oral or term paper) is chosen by the lecturer. An experimental examination (EA) for the practical part is generally required. The oral examination duration is stated in the general part of the examination regulations. The term paper must be at least 15 technical pages long. The experimental work consists of weekly assignment sheets with practice tasks.
